newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army sergeant in sex scandal gets 25 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army sergeant in sex scandal gets 25 years.

text.p: U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, convicted of 18 counts of rape involving six women trainees, was sentenced on Tuesday to 25 years in prison.
A military jury deliberated for 2-1/2 hours before sentencing Simpson. He was also sentenced to reduction in rank and forfeiture of pay, and was dishonarably discharged from the service.
Simpson, 32, last week was convicted of 18 counts of rape of six trainees in the first trial stemming from the sexual scandal at the military base.

Simpson, 32, was acquitted of one additional rape count last week, but found guilty of indecent assault. He also was found guilty of 25 of 35 other sexual misconduct counts against him, not guilty of seven and guilty of lesser offenses on three.

The drill sergeant could have faced life in prison for the rape convictions. He had pleaded guilty to 11 counts of consensual sex and five counts of propositioning, for which he faced a maximum sentence of 32 years in prison.
Simpson was the first of 12 trainers charged with various acts of misconduct at Aberdeen to go before a court-martial and was charged with the most rapes.
